t: Raid On The San Kwang Bookstore

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 1, Special Branch
REPORT
File No. SPECIAL POLICE
REGISTRY
No. Branch D. 8149/2
Date December 6, 1938.

Subject Raid on the San Kwang Bookstore (三光書局), 68 Rue Voyron,
on 23/11/38.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by C. Coombs

With reference to the query of D.C. (Special Branch)
on the attached copy of newspaper translation, I have to
report that careful enquiries show that the San Kwang
Bookstore, 68 Rue Voyron, which is owned by Ting Chuin-tao
(丁君匋), was raided by detectives attached to the
Political Section of French Police Headquarters on November
23, when some 200 books, chiefly of a political and anti-
Japanese nature were seized. Mr. Ting, who has severed
his connections with the publication of the local Chinese
daily known as the "News Digest," however, failed to secure
a Business Permit from the French Municipal Council before
starting business in the said bookstore.

A detailed report has been submitted to the French
Consular Authorities by the French Police who suggested that
a fine of $200 be imposed on the management of the bookstore
and that the seizure be confiscated, but no definite
instructions have yet been received by the French Police.

Details concerning Ting Chuin-tao's connections
with the "News Digest" were outlined in a Special Branch
report dated September 27, 1938. The allegation that he
is connected with the activities of the Chinese Communist
Party appear to be groundless.

Kuh Pao-hwa.
D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

报告
档案号：特别警察
登记处
编号：D股 8149/2
日期：1938年12月6日。

事由：1938年11月23日搜查位于维隆路（Rue Voyron）68号的三光书局。

由督察顾宝华（Kuh Pao-hwa）呈报，经C. Coombs转呈

兹就特务科副总监附来之报纸译文译本所询事项，经详细查访后报告如下：位于维隆路68号、由丁君匋（Ting Chuin-tao）所有的三光书局，于11月23日遭法国警察总局政治科所属侦探搜查，当场查获约200本书籍，主要具有政治性及反日性质。丁先生虽已切断其与本地中文日报《译报》（News Digest）出版工作的联系，但在该书店开业前，未能从法公董局取得营业执照。

法国警方已向法国领事当局提交详细报告，建议对该书店管理层处以200美元罚款，并没收查获物品，但法国警方尚未收到明确指示。

关于丁君匋与《译报》之关联详情，已在1938年9月27日之特务科报告中概述。指称其参与中国共产党活动之说，似无根据。

顾宝华
督察

特务科副总监

November 28, 1938. Morning Translation.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese owned Chinese language newspaper):

A "RUNNING DOG" OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY

With his experience of printing, Ting Chuin-tao (丁君匋), formerly chief of the Sales Department of the "Ta Kung Pao" (大公報) and at present one of the shareholders of the "News Digest" (譯報), has won the favour of the Communist Party and has been engaged as a "running dog" of the Party. It is due to his efforts that the "News Digest" has been published and maintained its existence up to the present.

On behalf of the Communist Party, Ting Chuin-tao recently edited and printed large quantities of propaganda matter, with a view to disseminating it in the Foreign Settlements. The matter came to the knowledge of certain authorities who despatched uniformed men and detectives to conduct a search at Ting's home where they found large quantities of Communist propaganda. Ting Chuin-tao was not placed under arrest nor was any penalty imposed on him. The public are greatly surprised at the attitude of these authorities. It is clear from this that these authorities are dealing leniently with the Communist Party.

(批：What about this?)
(批：A. J. Ral 8/11)
(批：29/11)

1938年11月28日。晨间译文。

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）：

共产党之“走狗”

丁君匋（Ting Chuin-tao），曾任《大公报》销售部主任，现为《译报》股东之一，凭借其在印刷方面的经验，博得共产党青睐，并被聘为该党之“走狗”。《译报》得以出版并维持至今，实赖其努力。

丁君匋近期代表共产党编辑并印制大量宣传品，意图在外国租界内散发。此事被某些当局获悉，遂派遣制服警员及侦探搜查丁宅，查获大量共产党宣传品。丁君匋未被逮捕，亦未受任何处罚。公众对这些当局的态度深感惊讶。由此可见，这些当局对共产党处理宽纵。

（批：此事如何？）
（批：A. J. Ral 11月8日）
（批：11月29日）
